title: General Knowledge
subject: general
year_note: Age hint 9. General knowledge is not a strand; the band is where the questions are answerable without being trivial.

questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Saudi Arabia?
questions.explanation: Riyadh is the capital and largest city of Saudi Arabia, in the centre of the country.

questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Pakistan?
questions.explanation: Many people guess Karachi, since it is Pakistan's biggest city, but the capital is actually Islamabad.

questions.prompt: Which city is the capital of the United Arab Emirates, even though many people assume it is Dubai?
questions.explanation: Abu Dhabi is the capital of the UAE. Dubai is more famous internationally, but it is not the capital.

questions.prompt: Belgium's capital, Brussels, is also the headquarters city for which major international organisation of European countries?
questions.explanation: Brussels hosts the main institutions of the European Union, as well as NATO's headquarters.

questions.prompt: South Africa is unusual in having how many capital cities, each handling a different role of government?
questions.explanation: South Africa has three capitals: Pretoria (administrative), Cape Town (legislative) and Bloemfontein (judicial).

questions.prompt: Which country's official capital is Dodoma, even though its largest and best known city is Dar es Salaam?
questions.explanation: Tanzania's official capital is Dodoma, though Dar es Salaam remains the country's largest city and main port.

questions.prompt: Which country has a national flag that is not a rectangle, but two triangular pennants stacked on top of each other?
questions.explanation: Nepal's flag is the only national flag in the world that is not a rectangle, made of two stacked triangular pennants.

questions.prompt: The flags of Australia and New Zealand both include a small Union Jack, honouring their history as former colonies of which country?
questions.explanation: Both flags carry the Union Jack in the corner as a link to their shared history as British colonies.

questions.prompt: Which river is usually considered the longest in the world, flowing through Egypt to the Mediterranean Sea?
questions.explanation: The Nile, flowing north through north east Africa, is usually considered the longest river in the world.

questions.prompt: Which mountain is the tallest above sea level in the world, found in the Himalayas?
questions.explanation: Mount Everest, on the border of Nepal and Tibet, is the highest mountain above sea level on Earth.

questions.prompt: The Amazon River flows mainly through which continent?
questions.explanation: The Amazon flows through several South American countries and carries more water than any other river in the world.

questions.prompt: Which is the largest hot desert in the world, covering much of northern Africa?
questions.explanation: The Sahara Desert stretches across much of northern Africa and is the world's largest hot desert.

questions.prompt: Which mountain range, running through several South American countries, is the longest mountain range on land?
questions.explanation: The Andes run down the western edge of South America and form the longest continuous mountain range on land.

questions.prompt: Which desert, found along the coast of Chile, is often called one of the driest places on Earth?
questions.explanation: The Atacama Desert in Chile is one of the driest places on Earth, with some areas that almost never see rain.

questions.prompt: Which cold, high desert covers a large area of Mongolia and northern China?
questions.explanation: The Gobi Desert is a cold desert, unlike the hot Sahara, and covers parts of Mongolia and northern China.

questions.prompt: Which river, flowing through China, is Asia's longest river?
questions.explanation: The Yangtze is the longest river in Asia and the third longest in the world, flowing through central China.

questions.prompt: How many continents are there, most commonly taught?
questions.explanation: The seven continents are usually listed as Asia, Africa, North America, South America, Antarctica, Europe and Oceania.

questions.prompt: Which is the largest ocean on Earth?
questions.explanation: The Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest ocean, covering more area than all the continents combined.

questions.prompt: Which continent is almost entirely covered by ice and has no permanent population?
questions.explanation: Antarctica is a continent almost entirely covered by ice, home only to scientists at research stations, not permanent residents.

questions.prompt: Which ocean lies between Africa, Asia and Australia?
questions.explanation: The Indian Ocean stretches between the east coast of Africa, southern Asia and Australia.

questions.prompt: Which continent is also a single country, and the smallest of the seven continents?
questions.explanation: Australia is unusual in being both a continent and a single country, and it is the smallest of the seven continents.

questions.prompt: Which two continents are joined on one continuous landmass, sometimes called Eurasia?
questions.explanation: Europe and Asia sit on one continuous landmass, so geographers sometimes refer to them together as Eurasia.

questions.prompt: Which scientist is famous for describing gravity, supposedly after watching an apple fall?
questions.explanation: Isaac Newton described the laws of motion and gravity in the late 1600s.

questions.prompt: Which scientist developed the theory of evolution by natural selection, after studying wildlife including on the Galapagos Islands?
questions.explanation: Charles Darwin published On the Origin of Species in 1859, explaining how species change over time through natural selection.

questions.prompt: Which scientist developed the theory of relativity and is famous for the equation E = mc²?
questions.explanation: Albert Einstein's theory of relativity, including the equation E = mc², changed how scientists understand space, time and energy.

questions.prompt: Which scientist's experiments with pea plants helped found the modern study of genetics?
questions.explanation: Gregor Mendel's careful experiments breeding pea plants in the 1800s revealed the basic rules of how traits are inherited.

questions.prompt: Which scientist discovered radioactivity alongside her husband, and was the first person to win Nobel Prizes in two different sciences?
questions.explanation: Marie Curie's research on radioactivity won her Nobel Prizes in both physics and chemistry.

questions.prompt: Which scientist's X-ray images were crucial evidence in working out the double helix structure of DNA?
questions.explanation: Rosalind Franklin's X-ray images of DNA gave vital clues that helped James Watson and Francis Crick work out its double helix structure.

questions.prompt: Which scientist developed an early vaccine against rabies and showed that heating liquids like milk could kill harmful germs, a process now named after him?
questions.explanation: Louis Pasteur developed the process now called pasteurisation and also created an early vaccine against rabies.

questions.prompt: Which scientist accidentally discovered a mould that killed bacteria in his lab, leading to the antibiotic penicillin?
questions.explanation: Alexander Fleming noticed in 1928 that a mould killed bacteria growing near it, leading to the development of penicillin.

questions.prompt: Which invention, credited to Johannes Gutenberg in the 1400s, allowed books to be produced much faster than by hand?
questions.explanation: Gutenberg's printing press, developed around the 1440s in Germany, made it possible to print many copies of a book far faster than copying by hand.

questions.prompt: Who is usually credited with patenting a practical telephone in the 1870s?
questions.explanation: Alexander Graham Bell patented a working telephone in 1876, though others were experimenting with similar ideas at the same time.

questions.prompt: Which invention, made practical by Thomas Edison and others in the late 1800s, gave people electric light in their homes?
questions.explanation: Edison and other inventors developed a long lasting, practical electric lightbulb in the late 1800s, changing how homes and streets were lit.

questions.prompt: The Wright brothers made history in 1903 by achieving what?
questions.explanation: Orville and Wilbur Wright achieved the first sustained, controlled flight of a powered aeroplane in 1903 in the United States.

questions.prompt: Roughly when was the World Wide Web invented, making the internet easy for ordinary people to use?
questions.explanation: Tim Berners-Lee developed the World Wide Web around 1989 to 1991, building a way to link and browse pages over the internet.

questions.prompt: Which ancient invention, first used for pottery before being used for transport, is considered one of the most important in human history?
questions.explanation: The wheel was first used to shape pottery, long before anyone thought to attach it to a cart for transport.

questions.prompt: Which ancient civilisation built the pyramids and the Sphinx, and was ruled by pharaohs?
questions.explanation: Ancient Egypt, along the Nile River, built enormous pyramids as tombs for its pharaohs thousands of years ago.

questions.prompt: Which ancient civilisation, based around the city of Rome, built a huge empire across Europe and controlled the Mediterranean?
questions.explanation: The Roman Empire grew from the city of Rome to control territory across Europe, North Africa and the Middle East.

questions.prompt: Ancient Greece is often credited with developing an early form of what system of government, where citizens could vote?
questions.explanation: Ancient Athens developed an early form of democracy, in which some citizens could vote directly on decisions.

questions.prompt: Which river valley civilisation, in what is now Iraq, is often called one of the earliest, and developed an early writing system called cuneiform?
questions.explanation: Mesopotamia, between the Tigris and Euphrates rivers, is often considered among the earliest civilisations, and its cuneiform writing is one of the first writing systems.

questions.prompt: The Indus Valley Civilisation, one of the world's earliest, grew up along a river now mainly running through which present day countries?
questions.explanation: The Indus Valley Civilisation flourished along the Indus River, in what is now mostly Pakistan and part of north west India.

questions.prompt: Which ancient civilisation in Central America is known for accurate calendar systems and step pyramids, and had a writing system only fully deciphered in recent times?
questions.explanation: The Maya civilisation, in what is now Mexico and Central America, built step pyramids and developed one of the most accurate calendars of the ancient world.

questions.prompt: What is the name of the star at the centre of our solar system, which the Earth orbits?
questions.explanation: The Sun is the star at the centre of our solar system, and every planet, including Earth, orbits it.

questions.prompt: What is the correct term for the huge collection of stars, including our Sun, that we belong to?
questions.explanation: Our Sun is one of hundreds of billions of stars in the Milky Way galaxy.

questions.prompt: Which of these correctly lists the four planets closest to the Sun, in order?
questions.explanation: Moving out from the Sun, the four rocky inner planets are Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars, in that order.

questions.prompt: What is the term for a large object, smaller than a full planet, that orbits the Sun but has not cleared its orbital path of other objects, like Pluto?
questions.explanation: Pluto is classified as a dwarf planet rather than a full planet because it has not cleared its orbit of other similarly sized objects.

questions.prompt: Judaism, Christianity and Islam are often grouped together because they all trace their origins back to which figure?
questions.explanation: Judaism, Christianity and Islam are often called the Abrahamic religions because each traces its roots back to Abraham.

questions.prompt: Which religion's central holy text is the Quran, believed by its followers to have been revealed to the Prophet Muhammad?
questions.explanation: The Quran is the central religious text of Islam, which followers believe was revealed to the Prophet Muhammad over about 23 years.

questions.prompt: Buddhism traces its origins to the teachings of a spiritual teacher known as the Buddha, who lived in which part of the world?
questions.explanation: The historical Buddha, Siddhartha Gautama, lived in what is now Nepal and northern India around 2,500 years ago.

questions.prompt: Jerusalem is considered a holy city by which three major world religions?
questions.explanation: Jerusalem holds deep religious significance for Jewish, Christian and Muslim traditions alike, each with important historic sites in the city.
